title: The `open` and `read` functions read the contents of a file as a string.

body: `open` is a function that opens a file, and `read` is a method that reads content from an open file as a string. title: "with" is a mechanism for safely opening and closing files.
when_to_show: When looking at the `with open(...) as f` structure
body: The `with` statement is a mechanism for safely using resources such as files. Within the `with open(...) as f:` block, you can read from or write to the file via `f`, and the file is automatically closed when the block ends. This reduces the likelihood of errors compared to code that explicitly uses `close`. When reading file-handling code, distinguish between what happens inside the `with` block and the fact that file usage has ended outside the block. title: pathlib's `Path` treats paths as building blocks
body: Path in pathlib allows you to handle file paths in a more structured way than using strings. When written as Path('data') / 'memo.txt', it can be interpreted as concatenating paths in a manner appropriate for the operating system. Path objects have attributes such as `name`, `suffix`, `stem`, and `parent`, making it easy to identify the filename, file extension, filename without the extension, and parent folder. body: Place code that might raise an error in the `try` block, and place code to be executed when an error occurs in the `except` block. title: Files and JSON are viewed in the order of reading, parsing, and using.
